text.p: Australian Opposition Treasury Spokesman Gareth Evans said on Wednesday that Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane was conservative on interest rates and that the bank needed to get the economy moving.

"With the government having abandoned any commitment to job growth and growth in the overall economy, there's really a huge responsibility on the Reserve to move things along as fast as possible," Evans told reporters.

"If the Reserve keeps a big leaden foot on the brake, meaning that the economy grows slower than it sustainably can, that's very bad news for jobs, and I'm disappointed that Mr Macfarlane has been so conservative."
Australian interest rates were high compared to other countries', he added.

Macfarlane, asked whether the bank could do more to bring down unemployment, said on Tuesday that the economy looked stronger now than it had last year and that the effect of last year's three monetary easings was coming through.
Evans did not elaborate on how the government had abandoned employment and economic growth.
The bank last year lowered its overnight cash-rate target from 7.5 percent, a recent peak, to 6.0 percent.
Until a few weeks ago, financial markets had anticipated a further cut but market interest rates now imply that an imminent easing is unlikely.
